\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{બગડવું} (bagaḍvũ)}{બગડવું (bagaḍvũ)}]{\gu{બગડવું} (bagaḍvũ) — to break down, to go bad}

\label{lesson:GU-C209-bagadvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for wheel, then the Gujarati for level crossing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{બગડવું}}
\textbf{\gu{બગડવું}} — \emph{bagaḍvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to break down, to go bad\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\gu{રસ્તામાં} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{બગડી}.} — \emph{rastāmā̃ gāḍī bagaḍī} — \textquotedblleft{}The car broke down on the way.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{બગડવું}} (\emph{bagaḍvũ}) goes back to Sanskrit \emph{vighaṭatē}, \textquotedblleft{}flies apart, is marred, is broken\textquotedblright{}, but CDIAL marks the Gujarati verb, glossed \textquotedblleft{}to be spoilt\textquotedblright{}, as borrowed from Hindi (CDIAL 11673).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for everyday life at A2.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bagaḍvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bagaḍvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rastāmā̃ gāḍī bagaḍī} — The car broke down on the way.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for wheel, then the Gujarati for level crossing, then say \emph{bagaḍvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ફસાવું} (phasāvũ)}{ફસાવું (phasāvũ)}]{\gu{ફસાવું} (phasāvũ) — to get stuck, to be trapped}

\label{lesson:GU-C209-phasavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to push, then the Gujarati for to collide.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ફસાવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ફસાવું}} — \emph{phasāvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to get stuck, to be trapped\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\gu{અમારી} \gu{ગાડી} \gu{ટ્રાફિકમાં} \gu{ફસાઈ}.} — \emph{amārī gāḍī ṭrāphikmā̃ phasāī} — \textquotedblleft{}Our car got stuck in traffic.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ફસાવું}} (\emph{phasāvũ}) is a tadbhava from the family that CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{spāśáyati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to be bound or stopped\textquotedblright{}, with Gujarati \emph{phā̃svũ} and \emph{phasāvvũ}, \textquotedblleft{}to ensnare\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13814).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to collide, then the Gujarati for to get stuck.
